messages:
mike: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on large-batch inference and a few GPU OOMs during the spike window (nightly 02:00). attaching short profiler dump and a couple observations.

anya: ok can you paste the snip? is it kv-prefill related or decode buffer growth?

mike: paste below. TL;DR: KV prefill dominates memory, fragmentation visible in allocator stats, and decode path triggers per-request overshoot when prefill+decode align.

mike: ```
PROFILE: pid=7821 time=2029-11-02T02:03:14Z
GPU 0: total 48GB used 41.2GB (fragments 6.7GB)
Allocator slabs: 256MB x 12, 64MB x 20, freelist high-water 3.2GB
KV cache: reserved 18GB, active 11.3GB, prefill 7.1GB, decode-owned 2.0GB
Requests: batch_size=48, seq=1024, avg_prefill_tokens=420
OOM events: 3 at 02:03:12, fallback to smaller model triggered
```

lee: yikes. Do we have per-request caps enabled? iirc prefill cap was 8GB last rollout.

mike: Caps were 8GB per-request prefill but we hit fragmentation so effective contiguous free blocks too small for decode staging buffers.

kaitlin: so fragmentation + high slab variety. any recent kernel selection changes? those can alter temp allocation patterns.

mike: yes, new fused-attn kernel landed last week — it reduces compute but temporarily increased intermediate buffer churn for long sequences. Profiling shows more short-lived 64MB allocations.

anya: sounds like allocator tuning required: larger uniform slab size or compaction. Can we try increasing big-slab count and enabling compaction on low-load windows?

lee: also suggests re-evaluating KV eviction policy — prefill-heavy workloads keep big contiguous blocks pinned. If we switch to size-aware eviction (prefer evicting large contiguous prefills) we might free contiguous space for decode.

mike: proposal: run two experiments A/B for next night: (A) reduce per-request prefill cap from 8GB->6GB and enforce per-request decode max of 1.5GB; (B) keep caps but enable aggressive slab compaction and increase 256MB slab pool by +4.

kaitlin: can we add a quick runtime metric to trace fragmentation (largest_free_contiguous / total_free)? would help quantify.

mike: added a quick gauge to runtime: largest_free_ratio. On the failing runs it drops to ~0.12 right before OOM. Normally sits >0.5.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: feature/allocator-experiments -> staging at 2029-11-02T15:12:00Z :rocket:

anya: good. for eviction, prefer a hybrid LRU-size policy: evict older prefills but prioritize those that release big contiguous ranges. avoids thrashing small cached entries.

lee: another idea: prefill fragmentation mitigation — allocate prefills from a separate pool of large contiguous slabs (pin-range) so decode buffers can use the main slab pool with compactable slabs. that separates lifetimes.

mike: that is promising but more invasive. short-term: run A/B, collect largest_free_ratio, OOM count, p99 latency, and fallback rate. if A reduces OOMs without latency regression, ship it.

kaitlin: logging checklist: which logs to capture? allocator histogram, KV-entry sizes, eviction decisions, kernel allocation traces (short-lived allocation count).

mike: capturing all those. also adding a small sampling profiler to capture stack of allocation origin for 10% of requests to see if fused-attn allocations correlate.

anya: thumbs up. timeline?

mike: start A/B tomorrow 02:00UTC, run 6 hours, will post summary. if A wins, we'll roll to prod with cap change + metrics. if not, try compaction change next week.

lee: thanks, keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
